thought.text: Found it — the field is `username`, not `login`. Let me redo the form login correctly with the right field name and fresh token.

reasoning_content: The field is `username`, not `login`. My earlier POST was using `login=admin`, so it was being sent with the username empty. Let me retry with `username=admin` and the correct authenticity_token (I need to fetch a new page and a new token tied to the session cookie — CSRF tokens in Rails are tied to the session, so I have to grab a fresh page and token with the same cookie jar).

action.command:
cd /tmp && rm -f op_cj2.txt
PAGE=$(curl -s -c op_cj2.txt http://localhost:8080/login)
TOKEN=$(echo "$PAGE" | grep -o 'name="authenticity_token" value="[^"]*"' | head -1 | sed 's/.*value="//;s/"$//')
echo "token_len=${#TOKEN}"
curl -s -b op_cj2.txt -c op_cj2.txt -o /tmp/login_resp.html -w 'POST /login: HTTP %{http_code}\n' -X POST http://localhost:8080/login \
  -H 'Origin: http://localhost:8080' -H 'Referer: http://localhost:8080/login' \
  --data-urlencode "authenticity_token=$TOKEN" \
  --data-urlencode "username=admin" \
  --data-urlencode "password=admin"
echo "--- follow session ---"
curl -s -b op_cj2.txt -c op_cj2.txt -o /tmp/projects.html -w 'GET /projects (authed): HTTP %{http_code} final=%{url_effective}\n' -L http://localhost:8080/projects
echo "--- projects page title ---"; grep -oE '<title>[^<]*</title>' /tmp/projects.html | head -1
echo "--- check admin logged in (look for admin name or sign out) ---"; grep -oiE 'Signed in as [^<]*|admin' /tmp/projects.html | head -3
